---
title: "Supplemental Materials"
subtitle: "Evaluating Open-Weight Large Language Models for Structured Depression Assessment from Clinical Interviews"
---

This site hosts the supplemental analysis reports and source code for:

> Girard, J. M., Kebe, G. Y., Morency, L.-P., De la Torre, F., Liebenthal, E., & Baker, J. T. (in press). Evaluating open-weight large language models for structured depression assessment from clinical interviews. *Journal of Psychopathology and Clinical Science*.

A preprint of the article is available on
[PsyArXiv](https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/63sw4).

## Archived Version

Frozen, citable copies of these materials are archived on Zenodo. The version
cited in the article is **v1.1.0**
([doi:10.5281/zenodo.23029765](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23029765)),
which adds the model predictions to the analysis code and reports archived in
v1.0.0.

[![](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.23029765.svg){fig-alt="DOI badge for version 1.1.0"}](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23029765)

## Analysis Reports

Each report is a rendered Quarto document containing the complete analysis code
and output. The corresponding source files (`.qmd`) are available in the
[source folder](https://github.com/jmgirard/llm-depression-assessment/tree/main/src).

| Report | Description |
|---|---|
| [Performance Analyses](analyses/performance_analyses.html) | Benchmarking of 25 open-weight LLMs on MADRS item and total score prediction; direct vs. indirect scoring comparison; error characterization |
| [Fairness Analyses](analyses/fairness_analyses.html) | Psychometric fairness audit (bias, sensitivity, precision) across sex, age, race, education, primary diagnosis, and interviewer |
| [Ablation Analyses](analyses/ablation_analyses.html) | Prompt ablation study isolating the contributions of descriptive and demonstrative cues |
| [Ensemble Analyses](analyses/ensemble_analyses.html) | Comparison of cross-model ensemble aggregation to the best single model |
| [Sample Demographics](analyses/demographics.html) | Participant and session descriptive statistics (Table 1) |

## Data Availability

The model predictions analyzed in this work are openly available in the
[data folder](https://github.com/jmgirard/llm-depression-assessment/tree/main/data),
with a codebook describing each file (CC BY 4.0).

The interview transcripts, human MADRS ratings, and participant
characteristics needed to reproduce the analyses are available to qualified
researchers through the NIMH Data Archive (NDA) in
[collection 3860](https://nda.nih.gov/edit_collection.html?id=3860) under an NDA Data Use Certification
([how to request access](https://nda.nih.gov/nda/access-data-info)). The public predictions link to these
records through their NDA subject identifiers; the codebook lists the NDA
structures and fields used. The interview recordings cannot be shared because
they contain identifiable protected health information from psychiatric
inpatients.
